title: Disprove hook-length identity (i) via n=2 counterexample

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Disproof of identity (i) (hook-length version is FALSE).**

Two parts:

**(C) Hook-multiset coefficient.** Show $[x^n]\,\text{LHS(i)}=\sum_{v\ge1}M_v(n)\,Q_v$, where $M_v(n):=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}H_v(\lambda)$ and $H_v(\lambda)=\#\{u\in\lambda:h_u=v\}$ is the number of cells of hook length $v$.

**(Counterexample).** Exhibit $(n,v)$ with $M_v(n)\ne R_v(n):=\sum_{m\ge1}p(n-vm)$. Smallest case $n=2$:
- $\lambda=(2)$ has hooks $\{2,1\}$; $\lambda=(1,1)$ has hooks $\{2,1\}$.
- Hence $M_2(2)=2$ and $M_1(2)=2$.
- But $R_2(2)=p(0)=1$ and $R_1(2)=p(1)+p(0)=2$.

So the coefficient of $Q_2x^2$ is $2$ on LHS(i) but $1$ on the RHS. By the independence of the $Q_v$ (see the coefficient-extraction issue), the two formal power series differ; therefore **(i) is false**.

Numerically, $M_v(n)\ne R_v(n)$ for every $n\in\{2,\dots,12\}$, so the failure is generic; one explicit instance suffices. The structural reason: every partition of $n\ge2$ contributes a hook of length $2$ in addition to parts equal to $2$, inflating the $v=2$ count beyond $R_2(n)$.
